transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-12 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Dana Cruz (Novara Head of Procurement), Ethan Li (Novara CISO), Priya Nair (Novara Corporate Counsel), Rosa Mendes (Novara Platform Eng)

Summary:
Quick kickoff between Redwood and Novara to align commercial and security path for onboarding. Focus areas: redlines to MSA/DPA, SLA appendix and latency SLOs, pilot benchmarking, and VPC/KMS path for Private deployment option. Agreed to a short pilot for 2 weeks and a redline turnaround timeline.

Topics covered:
- Contract redlines (MSA/DPA) and signatory limits
- SLA targets and uptime/latency measurements
- Pricing approval path and chargeback model (commits vs on-demand)
- Data residency, KMS/HSM and egress controls
- Pilot scope, benchmarks, and technical contacts

Transcript body:
[00:00] Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick intro — I'm Ava, AE on the account, Marcus is our SE. We'll walk through legal/commercial path and then Marcus will cover pilot and SLA appendix.
[00:12] Dana Cruz: Hi all, Dana here. We're trying to get procurement and legal aligned — Novara has some aggressive timeline to make a selection by end of Q2, so want to make sure legal path isn't the blocker.
[00:22] Marcus Patel: Hey Dana, yeah — totally. We'll try to surface the typical friction points early. On our side, common items are MSA redlines, DPA encryption/KMS language, and SLA appendix.
[00:35] Ethan Li: Quick note from security — we need clarity on data at rest encryption, customer-managed keys or Redwood-managed keys, and whether HSM-backed KMS is available. Also residency: some datasets must remain in EU.
[00:48] Priya Nair: And from legal, we need to confirm indemnity caps, breach notification timelines, and whether there's any subprocessor list. We'll look at the DPA and flag anything unusual.
[01:03] Ava Martinez: Great, so immediate ask: we'll send a proposed redlined MSA + DPA by next Thursday, March 19. That will include an SLA appendix for you to review. If you can flag the must-haves — like data residency and KMS style — we'll incorporate.
[01:20] Dana Cruz: That timeline should work if legal and security get what they need. Procurement will need an estimated TCO for both hosted and dedicated options, and an outline of commit pricing.
[01:33] Marcus Patel: For pricing, we typically show three paths: Hosted pay-as-you-go, Dedicated reserved capacity with monthly commit, and Private (VPC/on-prem) which has a platform fee + support. We can put together a TCO sheet with expected tokens and embedding units.
[01:46] Rosa Mendes: For Private deployments, we need specifics on network connectivity: VPC peering vs Transit Gateway, egress IP ranges, and whether Redwood supports private link. Also need to know if there are changes to latency guarantees when running in our VPC.
[02:05] Marcus Patel: On VPC, we support VPC peering and private link across regions. Latency SLOs are generally similar for Dedicated and Private, but exact numbers depend on region and instance sizing — that's what the SLA appendix will try to quantify. We'll propose a latency SLO of p95 < 200ms for typical 512-token workloads as a starting point, we can adjust based on your pilot.
[02:33] Ethan Li: p95 < 200ms is a helpful baseline but we need to test with our expected prompt distribution — some prompts are long and have KV cache patterns. We'll want to run benchmarks with our sample workload.
[02:46] Marcus Patel: Absolutely — we'll run your workload in a pilot. For that we need an infra contact and account IDs for VPC peering. Also we'll provide the benchmark harness and recommended runbook.
[03:00] Priya Nair: About the DPA, who is the subprocessor list? Do you use any third-party analytics or observability partners that have access to logs?
[03:10] Ava Martinez: We maintain a subprocessor list, yes — we'll include current vendors in the DPA. Observability data is retained in our platform; we have SOC 2 Type II reports and are working on a FedRAMP pathway for certain customers.
[03:24] Dana Cruz: SOC 2 is a baseline — some of our auditors will want FedRAMP scoped language for PHI-related workloads. Is there a FedRAMP timeline?
[03:34] Ava Martinez: We don't have FedRAMP cert yet for the hosted stack, but we do offer Private (on-prem/VPC) deployments where customers can meet FedRAMP controls in their environment. We can also discuss an SOC 2 plus focused controls mapping for your auditors.
[03:49] Ethan Li: OK. Regarding keys — does Redwood support BYOK with HSM-backed KMS? And can we rotate keys on our schedule?
[03:58] Marcus Patel: Yes, we support BYOK and customer-managed KMS via standard KMS integrations. Rotation policies can be aligned — we'll document allowed rotation windows. If you need HSM-backed stretch, we can discuss the Private deployment path and KMS/HSM tie-ins.
[04:17] Dana Cruz: Procurement needs to know escalation and signatory thresholds. Priya, do you have a sense of what you need?
[04:25] Priya Nair: We'll need to see the MSA to check liability caps and breach notice timing. Also please include a standard SLA credit mechanism — we usually require service credits for downtime beyond the SLO.
[04:37] Ava Martinez: We'll include a typical SLA credit formula in the appendix. For larger enterprise deals we can negotiate escalations and different caps — want to understand signatory limits so we can route approvals internally.
[04:50] Dana Cruz: Our procurement threshold is $250k without C-level signoff; above that, CFO approval required. If you can size the first-year commit we'll know the approval path.
[04:59] Marcus Patel: We'll produce a first-year TCO with two sizing scenarios: conservative and aggressive. That will feed your procurement routing.
[05:10] Rosa Mendes: On the pilot: we want a two-week pilot that covers both Gen chat requests and embeddings workload. We'll measure latency, throughput, and token cost. Can Redwood run the pilot using a dedicated pool or does it have to be hosted shared?
[05:26] Marcus Patel: For fidelity, Dedicated reserved pool is best but often we run initial pilots on a small dedicated instance or isolated tenancy in Hosted with capacity guarantees. We can do Dedicated pilot nodes for you to mirror production.
[05:39] Ethan Li: Also we need audit logs sent to our SIEM. Is there an option to forward logs or export events?
[05:47] Marcus Patel: Yes, we support log export to S3, and integration with common SIEMs — we'll include event types and retention details in the security annex.
[05:58] Dana Cruz: On pricing approvals: what documentation do you need from us to accelerate procurement?
[06:05] Ava Martinez: A shortlist of expected usage patterns (monthly tokens/embeddings), the pilot scope, and a confirmation of residency constraints. With those we can model commit tiers and show you the discount bands.
[06:18] Priya Nair: We'll also want to know about data deletion/retention — how long logs and prompts are kept, and whether Redwood can guarantee deletion on termination.
[06:28] Marcus Patel: We have configurable retention; deletion on contract termination is supported — we'll add clear language to the DPA.
[06:36] Ava Martinez: To wrap up, agreed items: we'll send redlined MSA/DPA + SLA appendix (Ava), Marcus will send pilot plan and perf spreadsheet, Novara will provide dataset/residency list and infra contact.
[06:48] Dana Cruz: Sounds good. If we get the redline by next week we can route legal and procurement and aim for pilot in two weeks.
[06:55] Rosa Mendes: I'll send AWS account IDs and a platform contact in a separate email after this call.
[07:02] Priya Nair: One more legal question offline — we may request a narrow indemnity carveout for regulated data. We'll flag that in the redline.
[07:12] Ava Martinez: Understood — we'll look for that and try to be pragmatic. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts.

End of transcript.
